title: Submission Integrity - Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Evidence
questionText: Rate the Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Evidence of the Submission Integrity dimension.
questionDescription: Use this dimension to decide whether the task can be meaningfully reviewed based on the submission itself. Focus on whether the task contains the minimum evidence needed to evaluate trajectories, rankings, and scores. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Evidence Gaps]; [All] [All] [Fail - Missing Core Evidence]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Missing Core Evidence]
Core task evidence is missing, corrupted, or too incomplete to determine whether the task was performed correctly.

[Non-Fail - Minor Evidence Gaps]
Minor pieces of context are missing (e.g., one non-critical note) but trajectories, rankings, and scores can still be reviewed end-to-end.
The task is fully reviewable and contains the required context, trajectories, consistency and evidence needed for a confident QC decision.

title: Submission Integrity - Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Consistency
questionText: Rate the Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Consistency of the Submission Integrity dimension.
questionDescription: See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor trajectory inconsistencies]; [All] [All] [Fail - Model Trajectory Consistency]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Trajectory Inconsistencies (4)]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Model Trajectory Consistency]
Annotator provides materially different information to models at equivalent milestones, giving one model an information advantage the other must discover independently.
¶NOTE: This does not include cases where a model has proactively addressed something – that is not counted as in informtion advatage for the other model.

[Non-Fail - Minor trajectory inconsistencies]
Minor framing differences at matching milestones that alter emphasis or level of detail but do not confer an information advantage.

[Non-Fail - Minor Trajectory Inconsistencies (4)]
Trivial wording differences at matching milestones that are semantically identical (pure rephrasing with no change in content or level of detail).
The trajectories are fully consistent

title: Submission Integrity - Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Prompt Matching
questionText: Rate the Task Reviewability / Core Evidence - Prompt Matching of the Submission Integrity dimension.
questionDescription: Differences in extra whitespace characters (such as '\n,' '\t', ' ', etc.) that do NOT affect the actual content of the prompts are acceptable. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply the error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Different Initial Prompts]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Different Initial Prompts]
The initial prompt across both models is not a perfect string-match.
The initial prompts across both models match exactly.

title: Submission Integrity - Task Scope / Feasibility
questionText: Rate the Task Scope / Feasibility of the Submission Integrity dimension.
questionDescription: A passing task should be coherent, realistically scoped, and feasible to complete through the Mailbox Ring workflow. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Scope Issues]; [All] [All] [Fail - Impossible Task]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Impossible Task]
The task cannot be completed with the provided setup, instructions, or environment.

[Non-Fail - Minor Scope Issues]
Scope is slightly too narrow or too broad but the task still supports a realistic milestone-based session.
Some instructions are ambiguous but a reasonable annotator can still guide the agent through the intended flow.
The task is appropriately scoped, feasible, and suitable for milestone-based agent interaction.

title: Trajectory Review - Milestone Achievement Verification
questionText: Rate the Milestone Achievement Verification of the Trajectory Review dimension.
questionDescription:
The annotator should only move to the next milestone after verifying that the current milestone was actually met. Do not rely on green markers, validator summaries, or completion text alone, the milestone completions must be supported by the trajectories. Non-Fail (3) covers two situations: (a) verification is indirect, e.g., agent output implies completion without explicit confirmation and the annotator could have run one extra check (test run, output inspection) to make it airtight; and (b) a milestone's structural continuation criterion (e.g., per-item commit count or stack order) is not fully met because of a model-side tooling/VCS side effect (e.g., per-item commit commands the tool collapses into a shared commit), while the substantive deliverable and the comparative signal between models remain reviewable. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.

¶ Exception:
- If a milestone was covered proactively by the model, i.e., Milestone 1 was sent, but the model covers Milestone 2 (even without it being sent) in this case, the annotator does not need to send Milestone 2 (it is fine if he sends it, but it's also fine if he doesn't send it).

¶ Note 07/17 - On Reviewability:
¶ For an error to impact reviewability, it has to actually degrade what a reviewer/eval can assess from the trajectory/code alone (client-facing defect).
¶ Example: A milestone requires "write unit tests before implementation," but the model writes the implementation first, then tests (misordered). If the tests still run and validate the final code correctly, the trajectory is still fully reviewable reviewer can see and judge every step so it's just a milestone-order slip, not a reviewability fail.

¶ Contrast: If the CB skips a milestone (e.g., never runs/shows the tests at all), so the reviewer has no way to verify the code actually works that missing evidence breaks reviewability, so it's a Fail.

¶ Even if the reason content is missing is an eng issue (e.g., trajectory got truncated so the code/tests never appear), it still fails reviewability because the reviewer can't assess it either way. The "cause" doesn't matter, only whether the trajectory can be judged
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Incorrect Milestone Pass]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Weak Verification]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incorrect Milestone Pass]
1+ milestones are skipped, misordered, or completed incorrectly in a way that materially invalidates the task outcome, the final ranking, or the reviewability (see notes) of the trajectory; The contributor continues prompting towards a later milestone before the agent successfully completes a preceding one.

[Non-Fail - Weak Verification]
Verification evidence exists but is indirect, or a substantially-attempted milestone is left imperfectly satisfied by a subtle implementation or tooling/VCS side effect while the trajectory remains reviewable.
Each claimed milestone is clearly supported by the observed interaction, outputs, or code state.

title: Trajectory Review - Trajectory Completeness
questionText: Rate the Trajectory Completeness of the Trajectory Review dimension.
questionDescription: A complete trajectory should include enough interaction to understand how the annotator worked through the task and reached completion. Provider-side encrypted model reasoning (encrypted chain-of-thought returned by the model provider, e.g., reasoningEncryptedContent blobs) is not authored content and does not count against completeness; only the visible interaction, tool calls/outputs, code, and final state are assessed. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Incomplete Trajectory]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Completeness Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incomplete Trajectory]
A required trajectory is missing, truncated, or clearly ends before the claimed completion state.

[Non-Fail - Minor Completeness Issues]
The trajectory is complete but slightly thin in one section (e.g., a milestone resolved in a single terse turn) while the overall flow remains interpretable.
A tool output is summarized rather than fully shown, but the outcome is still clear.
The trajectory is complete, interpretable, and sufficient for end-to-end review.

title: Trajectory Review - Prompting and Interaction Discipline - Natural Prompting
questionText: Rate the Prompting and Interaction Discipline - Natural Prompting of the Trajectory Review dimension.
questionDescription: Mailbox Ring expects natural prompting. Annotators may use suggested prompts as inspiration, but should not over-index on them or reduce the interaction to a script. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Scripted / Artificial Interaction]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Interaction Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Scripted / Artificial Interaction]
The interaction is clearly robotic, formulaic, or over-dependent on canned prompts and the auditor fails to flag it.

[Non-Fail - Minor Interaction Issues]
One or two follow-ups sound slightly templated, but the overall session still reads as natural and purposeful.
Persona use is inconsistent in a minor way but does not break immersion or guidance quality.
The interaction feels natural, purposeful, and consistent with the project's goal of capturing real coder preferences.

title: Trajectory Review - Prompting and Interaction Discipline - Guidance
questionText: Rate the Prompting and Interaction Discipline - Guidance of the Trajectory Review dimension.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - No Real Guidance]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - No Real Guidance]
The annotator does not meaningfully guide the agent toward milestones, yet the task is treated as acceptable.
Prompts contain sufficient guidance that the annotator is guiding the agent towards the milestones.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Subjective Ranking Quality
questionText: Rate the Subjective Ranking Quality of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription: The ranking should reflect the annotator's actual preference between trajectories. It is a vibe check, not a formula. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Ranking Contradicts Evidence]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Ranking Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Ranking Contradicts Evidence]
The final ordering is not defensible given the rationale and observed trajectories.

[Non-Fail - Minor Ranking Issues]
The ranking is plausible overall but the gap between two adjacent trajectories feels under-justified.
The ordering reads slightly too aligned with the global scores rather than as a genuine preference call, yet is still defensible.
The ranking clearly reflects subjective preference and is plausible given the trajectories.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Trajectory Summaries - Specificity
questionText: Rate the Trajectory Summaries - Specificity of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription: The per-trajectory summaries should be factually accurate, opinionated and specific, not neutral placeholders. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Generic Summary]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Summary Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Generic Summary]
One or more trajectory summaries are vague, templated, or provide no concrete commentary.

[Non-Fail - Minor Summary Issues]
Summaries are opinionated but include a bit of neutral recap.
Each summary is opinionated, concrete, and tied to the observed model behavior.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Trajectory Summaries - Completeness
questionText: Rate the Trajectory Summaries - Completeness of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription: The per-trajectory summaries should be factually accurate, opinionated and specific, not neutral placeholders. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Missing Summary Content]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Summary Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Missing Summary Content]
A required summary field is absent or too incomplete to be useful.

[Non-Fail - Minor Summary Issues]
One summary is slightly shallower than the others but still references concrete model behavior.
Each summary is opinionated, concrete, and tied to the observed model behavior.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Trajectory Summaries - Accuracy
questionText: Rate the Trajectory Summaries - Accuracy of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription:
The per-trajectory summaries should be factually accurate, opinionated, and specific, not neutral placeholders. 

¶¶A single mislabeled secondary detail of a real, observed event (Non-Fail, not Fail) is one where the event genuinely happened and only its type/timing/milestone-index label is imprecise, e.g., calling a segmentation fault hit during compilation a 'bug' or saying the model 'edited' a file it actually created (action mislabeled) so the ranking and score are unaffected. 
¶¶For all options except the last, apply the error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Fabricated Claims]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Fabricated Claims]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Fabricated Claims]
A summary or rationale field contains a specific technical claim – event, output, or behavior – that is contradicted by or absent from the trajectory evidence.

[Non-Fail - Fabricated Claims]
Summaries or rationale mislabel secondary details (the type, timing, or milestone index) of more than one real, observed event without changing the ranking or the score. This does not apply to fabricated events or cross-model misattribution, which remain Fail.

[Non-Fail - Fabricated Claims]
A single secondary detail (type, timing, or milestone index) of one real, observed event is mislabeled; all other content is accurate, and the ranking and score are unaffected. This does not apply to fabricated events or cross-model misattribution, which remain Fail.
Each summary is opinionated, concrete, and tied to the observed model behavior.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Final Comparative Rationale - Reasoning
questionText: Rate the Final Comparative Rationale - Reasoning of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription: The final field should explain how the annotator weighed the important criteria and reached the ordering. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues]; [All] [All] [Fail - No Comparative Reasoning]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues (4)]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - No Comparative Reasoning]
The rationale does not explain how the final ranking was reached.

[Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues]
The rationale explains the ordering but leans on multiple generic phrases instead of specific trajectory evidence.

[Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues (4)]
The rationale is specific and evidence-grounded except for a single generic phrase.
The rationale clearly shows how the annotator compared the trajectories and why the final ordering makes sense.

title: Ranking & Rationale - Final Comparative Rationale - Evidence
questionText: Rate the Final Comparative Rationale - Evidence of the Ranking & Rationale dimension.
questionDescription: The final field should explain how the annotator weighed the important criteria and reached the ordering. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Unsupported Comparative Claim]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Unsupported Comparative Claim]
The rationale makes major claims that are not grounded in the observed trajectories.

[Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues]
Multiple comparison points are supported indirectly rather than with concrete examples or a combination of indirect support and mislabeled details of real, observed events without driving the final ordering.

[Non-Fail - Minor Rationale Issues (4)]
A single comparison point is supported indirectly rather than with a concrete example, OR a single non-load-bearing comparison point mislabels the type or timing of a real, observed event; everything else is concretely grounded, and the ordering is unaffected.
The rationale clearly shows how the annotator compared the trajectories and why the final ordering makes sense.

title: Global Scores - Correctness Score
questionText: Rate the Correctness Score of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: Correctness is primarily concerned with the final solution or end state. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Incorrect Correctness Score]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Correctness Scoring Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incorrectness Correctness Score]
The assigned score does not match the final code, output, or verified end state, and the difference in score is 2+ points (1<>3 or 3<>1)

[Non-Fail - Minor Correctness Scoring Issues]
The assigned score does not match the final code, output, or verified end state, and the difference in score is 1 point (1<>2, 2<>3 or vice-versa)
The score is in the right range but does not fully reflect a minor edge case the solution handled or missed.
A small end-state nuance is under-weighted but the overall score direction is defensible.
The score accurately reflects the final solution's correctness.

title: Global Scores - Agent Behavior Score
questionText: Rate the Agent Behavior Score of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: Consider decision-making, planning, tool usage, exploration, and instruction following throughout the trajectory. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Incorrect Agent Behavior Score]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Agent Behavior Scoring Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incorrect Agent Behavior Score]
The score does not match the observed planning, execution, or tool-use behavior, and the difference in score is 2+ points (1<>3 or 3<>1)

[Non-Fail - Minor Agent Behavior Scoring Issues]
The score does not match the observed planning, execution, or tool-use behavior, and the difference in score is 1 point  (1<>2, 2<>3)
The score captures the overall behavior but slightly under- or over-weights a specific planning or tool-use moment.
A strong/weak intermediate moment is acknowledged in the rationale but only partially reflected in the score.
The score accurately captures how the agent behaved during the interaction.

title: Global Scores - (Optional) Code Style Score - Rating
questionText: Rate the (Optional) Code Style Score - Rating of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: If the task does not require code, it can be skipped. If assessing the code would take more than ~10 minutes, cbs skim through some of the files to assess the model's general style. If one or more agents unnecessarily produce huge amounts of code, cbs may flag verbosity without reviewing every line. The ranking value is optional, but there must be a rationale that justifies why it was not ranked. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Incorrect Code Style Score]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Code Style Scoring Issues]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incorrect Code Style Score]
The code style score does not fit the visible quality of the final output, and the difference in score is 2+ points (1<>3 or 3<>1)

[Non-Fail - Minor Code Style Scoring Issues]
The code style score does not fit the visible quality of the final output, and the difference in score is 1 point (1<>2, 2<>3)
The score is defensible but could be justified with more specific code references.
The reviewer handles this dimension correctly: either scores it well with clear justification or skips it for the right reason.

questionText: Rate the (Optional) Code Style Score - Improperly Completed of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: If the task does not require code, it can be skipped. [Non-Fail - Minor Code Style Scoring Issues]

title: Global Scores - (Optional) Code Style Score - Improperly Omitted
questionText: Rate the (Optional) Code Style Score - Improperly Omitted of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: If the task does not require code, it can be skipped. If assessing the code would take more than ~10 minutes, cbs skim through some of the files to assess the model's general style. If one or more agents unnecessarily produce huge amounts of code, cbs may flag verbosity without reviewing every line. The ranking value is optional, but there must be a rationale that justifies why it was not ranked. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.

title: Global Scores - Communication Score
questionText: Rate the Communication Score of the Global Scores dimension.
questionDescription: Consider clarity, summaries, responsiveness, and whether the agent communicated effectively with the annotator. See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply an error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Communication Scoring Issues]; [All] [All] [Fail - Incorrect Communications Score]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Incorrect Communications Score]
The score does not match the clarity or usefulness of the agent's communication, and the difference in score is 2+ points (1<>3 or 3<>1)

[Non-Fail - Minor Communication Scoring Issues]
The score does not match the clarity or usefulness of the agent's communication, and the difference in score is 1 point (1<>2, 2<>3)
The score captures overall communication quality but under-weights one moment of unclear messaging or a particularly strong summary.
A minor responsiveness issue is noted in the rationale but not fully reflected in the numeric score.
The score accurately reflects the quality and effectiveness of the agent's communication.

title: Justification - Support Claims - Accuracy
questionText: Rate the Support Claims - Accuracy of the Justification dimension.
questionDescription:
A single trivially mislabeled detail is Non-Fail (not Fail) when the primary, score-supporting claim stays accurate and the score is unchanged; e.g., the justification calls a segmentation fault encountered during compilation a 'bug' or describes a real compile failure as a 'runtime error' (wrong error type) while the point it supports still holds: the observation is grounded in the trajectory and only the label is imprecise. For all options except the last, apply the error category.

¶¶Note: This error applies to the rationale/justifications provided for the Global Grading Criteria scores.


¶¶See the spec doc for examples. For all options except the last, apply the error category.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Claims Inaccurate]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Claims Inaccurate]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Claims Inaccurate (4)]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Claims Inaccurate]
1 or more primary claims (claims that directly support the assigned score) are inaccurate, OR inaccurate secondary claims are material enough to change the assigned score.

[Non-Fail - Claims Inaccurate]
Multiple secondary or illustrative claims are inaccurate (e.g., misattributed examples or mislabeled details), or a single secondary claim's inaccuracy goes beyond a trivial mislabeled detail, while the primary claim that supports the assigned score is accurate and the score itself is unchanged.

[Non-Fail - Claims Inaccurate (4)]
A single secondary or illustrative claim contains a trivial inaccuracy (e.g., one mislabeled detail), all other claims are accurate, and the assigned score is unchanged.
All claims being made are accurate

title: User Messages - Milestone JSON Leakage
questionText: Do any of the user messages include any of the raw milestone JSON?
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - Milestone Leakage]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Milestone Leakage]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Milestone Leakage]
The raw milestone was completely leaked in one of the user turns

[Non-Fail - Milestone Leakage]
A small portion of the raw milestone is leaked in any of the user turns. (E.g., M2: Add a --report flag that generates a batch summary.)
No raw milestone information has leaked in any of the user turns.

title: All CB Generated Content - Spelling / Grammar - Major Error
questionText: Rate the Spelling / Grammar - Major Error of the All CB Generated Content dimension.
questionDescription: Note: This does NOT apply this criterion to prompts sent in the agent interactions.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Fail - SGP Major Error]; [All] [All] [Non-Fail - SGP Minor Error]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - SGP Major Error]
Has 4 or more spelling (minor) or grammar errors. 

¶ Note: For spelling/grammar, errors accumulate across the entire task. For example, if the prompt had 2 spelling errors and the response had 2 spelling  errors, we'd fail the task

[Non-Fail - SGP Minor Error]
Has 2-3 spelling/grammar errors

[Non-Fail - SGP Minor Error]
Has exactly 1 minor spelling, grammar, or punctuation error (e.g., a single word is plural instead of possessive).
There are no easily discernible errors

title: All CB Generated Content - Spelling / Grammar - Egregious Errors
questionText: Rate the Spelling / Grammar - Egregious Errors of the All CB Generated Content dimension.
questionDescription: Note: This does NOT apply this criterion to prompts sent in the agent interactions.
errorCategories: [All] [All] [Non-Fail - Minor Egregious Spelling Error]; [All] [All] [Fail - Multiple Egregious Spelling Errors]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - Multiple Egregious Spelling Errors]
Has 2 or more egregious spelling errors
¶ Note: For spelling, grammar, and punctuation, errors accumulate across the entire task. For example, if the prompt had 2 spelling errors and the response had 2 spelling  errors, we'd fail the task

[Non-Fail - Minor Egregious Spelling Error]
Has 1 egregious spelling error

title: All CB Generated Content - Original Work - Cheating
questionText: Rate the Original Work - Cheating of the All CB Generated Content dimension.
questionDescription: The content contains clear and obvious evidence of unsanctioned LLM usage, shown by concrete artifacts such as hallucinated or trajectory-contradicted content, copy-paste leakage (assistant preambles, prompt scaffolding, or markdown the contributor did not author), or text that is inconsistent with the observed trajectory. Note: Style alone is not sufficient for a Fail. Verbosity, polished prose, parallel paragraph structure across the two model evaluations, and occasional pleasantries are NOT cheating when the content is specific and grounded in the trajectory. See the spec doc for examples.
errorCategories: [Core Dimensions] [Original Work] [Fail - LLM Cheating]; [Core Dimensions] [Original Work] [Non-Fail - Suspected LLM Cheating]
answerOptionText:
[Fail - LLM Cheating]
The content contains clear and obvious evidence of unsanctioned LLM usage in their work
¶ Note: Evidence of chatbot usage could be excessive usage of fluff / pleasantries, generic responses, lack of human understanding and nuance, etc. Copy paste prompts that ask for summaries or analysis of the pasted material are okay.

[Non-Fail - Suspected LLM Cheating]
The content shows evidence of unsanctioned LLM usage or otherwise appears unnatural, but it is not obvious that an LLM was used to generate their work.
The content does not contain clear or obvious evidence of LLM usage.
